faq: Is Glyph Jot really free?
Yes. There is no paid tier, no subscription and no word or minute limit.
Does my voice leave my Mac?
No. Speech is turned into text by Apple's on-device model, and summaries and clean-up use Apple Intelligence on the Mac. Glyph Jot makes no network requests.
Does a bot join my calls?
No. Click Record and it records your microphone and the Mac's sound. Nobody in the call sees a notetaker join.
Should I tell people I am recording?
Yes. Follow the consent rules where you and the other people are. Glyph Jot records what your Mac hears; asking first is up to you.
Does it work offline?
Yes. Dictation, recording, transcripts and summaries all run on the Mac, with or without a connection.
Where are my notes kept?
In a folder on your Mac that you choose, an Obsidian vault too. Notes are Markdown files, dictations are lines of JSON, and recordings are plain folders with an .m4a file.
What do I need?
An Apple silicon Mac on macOS 26 or later. Summaries, Command Mode and asking your history need Apple Intelligence; plain dictation and recording do not.
Is there an iPhone app?
The Glyph app and the Glyph keyboard are in TestFlight testing, not on the App Store yet.
How is it different from Wispr Flow or Granola?
They work in their cloud and need an account. Glyph Jot does dictation and meetings in one app, on your Mac, with no account. See Compare for each app side by side, with sources.

faq: Is Glyph Time free?
Yes. There is no paid tier and no subscription.
Does it watch everything I do?
No. A session keeps only the project name and the app in front, never a window title, a URL or anything you typed. Tracking apps and tabs is a separate switch you turn on.
Where is my time kept?
As plain lines in a folder you choose. Each Mac writes its own file, so a synced folder never conflicts.
What if I walk away?
Five minutes without a key or the pointer, a locked screen or a sleeping Mac pause the clock.
Can I export it?
Yes, a period as CSV or Markdown, beside the session files.
Is there an iPhone app?
Glyph Time on iPhone is in testing, not on the App Store yet.
What do I need?
An Apple silicon Mac on macOS 26 or later.

faq: Is Glyph Rig free?
Yes, free and open source under the MIT license.
Which agents does it run?
Claude Code, Codex, AGY, Cursor, Crush, Cortex, OpenCode and pi, and any other command-line agent you add in one line.
Does it phone home?
No network requests except glyph update, glyph usage --live and the GitHub star you agree to.
Where does it work?
In zsh, with tmux, Herdr, Zellij, WezTerm or a bare shell.
How do I install it?
Clone the repo and source install.sh: one file into ~/.config/glyph and one line into ~/.zshrc. glyph update fetches the latest.
What was it called before?
Glyph Code, until October 2026. Same tool and same glyph command.

faq: Is Glyph Arena free?
Yes. Glyph Native installs it and keeps it up to date, and the engine that runs every test is open source (GPL-3.0). Cloud model calls are billed by their providers, under a monthly cap you set.
Which models can it test?

Every model your installed tools reach: Claude Code, Codex, the Gemini CLI, Ollama on this Mac and your other Macs, and image and voice models through the API keys you already have. Each effort level can enter on its own.
What do Clear, Leaning and Coin flip mean?

Two models are compared on the tests both took. Clear means the record would almost never happen by chance (six straight wins or better). Leaning means more tests could settle it. Coin flip means nothing separates them yet.
Are health and money questions sent to the cloud?
No. Those areas run only on models on your own Macs, refused before any call.
What if two models keep tying?
When both score near the top, the tests are too easy. Arena says so and asks for a harder test, instead of running more of the same.

faq: What is Glyph?
A family of apps for your agentic life, made by fru.dev: Glyph Bot, Jot, Ibis and Rig, and the tools around them.
Is it free?
Yes. Every Glyph app is free.
Where is my data?
In files you own: your Mac, or a vault folder you choose. fru.dev runs no server for the apps.
Is it open source?
Glyph Bot, its engine and Glyph Rig are open source on GitHub. Every other app is free, and its code is private for now.
How do I install the apps?
Install Glyph Native. It installs each app and keeps it up to date, signed and notarized by Apple.
What do I need?
An Apple silicon Mac; most apps need macOS 26 or later. iPhone apps are in testing.
